column3: The solution works only at a small scale.
column4: Check how cost, queues, and stored data grow with input in the design or code.
Look for nested loops, repeated scans, or searches over growing data on paths that matter.

column3: N+1 queries, unnecessary I/O, or repeated network calls.
column4: Look for queries, I/O, or network calls inside loops that one batched call would serve.

column3: Unbounded allocations, leaks, or missing streaming.
column4: Look for collections, buffers, or caches that grow without bound, and whole-input reads where streaming fits.

column3: Contention, serialization, deadlock, or starvation prevents required throughput or latency.
column4: Look for locks held across slow work, shared hot spots, and waits that can block each other.

column3: Blocking the event loop or UI thread.
column4: Look for blocking I/O, waits, or long computations on the event loop or UI thread.

column3: Retries amplify load or cancelled work keeps consuming resources.
column4: Check that retries back off and stop, and that cancelled work releases its resources.
Check that each cache is invalidated when its inputs change.

column3: A benchmark is unrepresentative or has no baseline.
column4: Check that the recorded benchmark states its data, environment, and baseline, and separates cold start from steady operation where relevant.

column3: An optimization breaks behavior or adds unjustified complexity.
column4: Check that the worker's recorded tests cover the optimized behavior and that the added complexity is justified by the measured gain.

column3: An average hides unacceptable latency for some operations.
column4: Check that the recorded results report the percentiles the requirement depends on, not only an average.

column3: Work can arrive faster than it is processed and the backlog grows without bound.
column4: Where work arrives from outside, look for a bound or admission control on its queue.

column3: A short measurement misses degradation during sustained operation.
column4: Where sustained operation matters, check the recorded measurement ran long enough to show growth in latency or resource use.

column3: An optimization moves cost outside the measured section.
column4: Check that the measured section includes preparation, background work, and cleanup, not only the optimized part.

column3: An apparent improvement is measurement noise.
column4: Check that the recorded improvement was repeated and exceeds the run-to-run variation.
